story.title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts

draft:
A hardware wallet just turned into a spying device.  

Ledger has confirmed that a malicious chip was inserted into some of its devices, allowing attackers to siphon private keys and steal crypto. The breach isn’t a software bug—it’s a supply‑chain compromise that defeats the very premise of “cold storage.”

What this tells me is that trust in hardware now hinges on provenance as much as on encryption. Even a single rogue component can bypass all the layers of defense we build around a wallet. It also raises the bar for auditors: we need forensic checks that go beyond firmware signatures and actually verify the silicon.

I’m rethinking how I source and inspect any security‑critical hardware, and I’m curious—what steps are you taking to ensure the physical integrity of the devices you rely on?
